dispositions.justification: Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency with AI-first completion. Global style operations remain validated and scoped; eligible inspected design edits may auto-apply with Undo, while source-bound proposals remain manual.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency without restoring request-text classification. Field validation and protected bindings remain enforced; pointer, format, kind and barcode patch keys remain outside automatic application.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Added fields still pass typed authoring, selected-scope and original-binding checks. Automatic application remains restricted to permitted nonbinding static or image additions.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Removal remains a validated scoped operation, and original protected identities remain checked if reinstated. Removing a field with an existing pointer still requires human application.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Reordering still requires the complete unique existing field identity set and selected-scope authorization; AI-first answer selection does not bypass those checks.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Section patches remain limited to supported keys and valid section targets, with scope and final design validation retained before proposal delivery.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Section reordering still requires the exact supported section set and remains subject to scope checks; only eligible inspected ordinary design proposals can auto-apply.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency without changing page authority. Page patches retain final design validation and are absent from the automatic-operation allowlist, so human Preview and Apply remain required.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Logo authoring still accepts supported existing assets or removal, remains scoped, and grants no asset import or approval authority under AI-first completion.
Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Collection selection still requires an available array binding and protected-binding validation, and remains excluded from automatic application.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Heading edits remain typed and scoped and do not enable the header implicitly. AI-first completion changes answer selection, not heading visibility or commit guards.

Reconciles shared contract changes and removal of TABLE_BACKGROUND_INTENT. The host no longer interprets requested row-fill intent, but supported color validation, table scope, inspection and automatic-application exclusions remain.

Reconciles the changed shared contract dependency. Element typography remains restricted to supported targets and schema bounds, with selected-scope checks and inspected automatic application retaining Undo.

The changed registry and effect profiles now expose both answer and proposal tools under design authority regardless of request wording. Capability discovery does not itself grant source access or satisfy answer evidence.

The changed bundled form-authoring guide explicitly describes AI-first answer versus proposal selection. Reading a guide remains evidence for an answer, not an additional effect or source-workspace authorization.

The changed shared registry and handler closure accompanies request-independent design grants. Context still carries measured typography and host-selected design or source commit guidance; the host no longer replaces the resulting model answer.

The changed effect and handler closure permits the agent to choose edits without host text classification. Operations still affect only the private draft, enforce parser and scope guards, and invalidate inspection and observation evidence.

Reconciles the changed shared handler and registry closure. Inspection still captures host-owned evidence for the exact candidate; finish requires that latest receipt and ready diagnostics, independently of AI-selected request handling.

Reconciles the changed shared registry and guide closure without expanding disclosure. Semantic observation still requires host authorization, replaces current evidence and clears final inspection, so finish requires a subsequent inspect_draft.

Reconciles the changed registry and panel dependency closure. Page retrieval remains bound to the latest observation and independent pixel authorization; AI-first answer selection supplies neither capture permission nor asset approval.

Reconciles the changed shared registry and handler closure. Scenario diagnostics remain answer evidence but do not establish run.inspected and cannot replace inspection of the exact final candidate before finish.

Reconciles the changed shared handler and effect closure. Undo still retracts only a private draft step, invalidates inspection and observation evidence, and requires fresh inspection before proposal completion.

Reconciles the changed shared registry and AI-first guide dependency. Notes remain bounded replacement memory for the current run and provide no additional edit, disclosure, proposal approval or commit authority.

The changed contract removes TABLE_BACKGROUND_INTENT, not deterministic proposal guards. Finish still requires nonempty changes, original protected bindings and the latest ready inspection; coding proposals additionally require current imported artifact lineage.

Replaces the obsolete classifier and answer-effect-removal disposition. Design and coding grants retain answer; completion preserves the exact model message and returns answered after evidence and freshness checks. Only finish delivers a proposal.

Reconciles changed orchestration and shared registry guidance. The agent may report an actual missing capability, but human Preview and Apply alone are not blockers. Reporting a blocker delivers and applies no proposal.

Reconciles changed source orchestration: explicit one-run consent, not request wording, selects the existing source lease. Listing remains run-owned, and sourceBound propagation prevents automatic application of resulting proposals.

Reconciles the changed registry and source-run closure. Bounded UTF-8 reads remain lease-authorized and untrusted; removing request-text classification does not grant business-data disclosure or automatic source application.

Reconciles the changed source orchestration dependency. Search remains bounded to the authorized fictional workspace, and its results cannot change the host-owned sourceBound flag or bypass manual application.

Reconciles request-independent source profile selection under explicit consent. Existing-file writes still require exact digests and a genuine lease, never directly change the live form, and retain source-bound manual application.

Reconciles the changed registry and panel closure. Exact-hash atomic patch semantics remain; source-bound proposals are excluded both when automatic application is selected and at the final autoApply entry point.

Reconciles changed source orchestration without expanding command authority. Execution still requires the existing genuine coding lease and isolated runner contract; stdout or exit zero is not independent acceptance. Runtime execution is UNVERIFIED.

Reconciles the changed source-run dependency closure. Diff remains a read of changes against the original fictional starter, not approval or commit permission; resulting source proposals remain excluded from automatic application.

Reconciles the changed registry and panel closure. Artifact retrieval still requires an authorized workspace and successful current command lineage, returns an opaque source-bound descriptor, and cannot authorize automatic application.

Reconciles the changed source orchestration closure. Verified artifact operations still enter the same private draft parser and binding guards, invalidate inspection, and require fresh inspection plus explicit human application.

The guide now states AI-first completion instead of classifier narrowing, answer-effect removal or current draft-not-produced outcomes. Scope, schemas, protected bindings, exact inspection, disclosure and commit guards remain deterministic.

Reconciles the changed shared knowledge-loader dependency included in this entry's closure. Human-mediated and unavailable workflows remain distinct from callable tools, and AI-first completion adds no commit or unavailable workflow authority.

Reconciles the changed shared knowledge-loader dependency. The guide's read-only restriction remains valid for explicit host read-only profiles, not a claim that question wording selects authority. Finish_answer still produces no draft.

Reconciles changed source consent consumption and AI-first orchestration dependencies. Genuine lease and artifact lineage remain required, while sourceBound propagation, workspace policy rejection and final autoApply rejection preserve human application.
